brief.headline: Samsung earnings print Tuesday + SK ADR 7/10 converge with HBM4 ramp divergence; July DRAM/NAND QoQ still +13-18% despite Q2 parabola fatigue
brief.summary: <cite index="41-1,41-3,41-4">Samsung Electronics is widely expected to post record-high earnings on Tuesday with revenue consensus around 170 trillion won and operating profit of 86 trillion won, some estimates topping 90 trillion won</cite>. <cite index="34-3">SK Hynix begins Nasdaq ADR trading July 10</cite>, but <cite index="34-15,34-17">both names tumbled 9-15% on Thursday, tracking Nasdaq tech selloff</cite>. <cite index="3-10,3-11">Samsung began HBM4 mass production February 2026 and crossed $1 billion cumulative HBM4 revenue by June</cite>, while <cite index="3-1,3-2,3-7">SK Hynix is delaying some HBM3E-to-HBM4 line conversions, retooling capacity for DDR5 instead</cite>, exploiting <cite index="3-4">DDR5 operating margins approaching 90%</cite>. <cite index="13-1">Q3 conventional DRAM contract pricing still rising 13-18% QoQ, NAND up 10-15%</cite>, decelerating from Q2's 58-63% DRAM / 70-75% NAND jumps but signaling no near-term peak.
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix structurally long on HBM share (62% market, 70% of NVDA Rubin HBM4 allocation per UBS) but tactically exposed to ADR execution risk and DDR5 margin harvest telegraphing HBM4 supply discipline. Samsung compressed on HBM3E qualification lag but now first-mover on HBM4 mass production with $1B+ revenue run-rate and AMD MI455X / Google TPU wins. Relative: fade SK on ADR pop if volume light; accumulate Samsung into earnings if print ≥90T won confirms HBM4 monetization velocity exceeds street model. Both vulnerable to hyperscaler capex fatigue headlines but insulated by 2027 fab lag (Micron Singapore, SK M17, Samsung P5 all post-2027).

memory_cycle.stage: Late expansion, decelerating but not peaking
memory_cycle.notes: Q1 2026 DRAM contracts +93-98% QoQ (record), Q2 +58-63%, Q3 forecast +13-18%. NAND accelerated Q2 (70-75%) vs Q1 (55-60%), now cooling to 10-15% Q3. HBM capacity sold out through 2026; conventional DRAM supply constrained by HBM wafer reallocation (3:1 conversion ratio). Buyers balking at spot but contract pricing still rising. New capacity not meaningful until late 2027 (SK M15X, Micron Idaho) or 2028 (Samsung P5). Cycle durability driven by AI infrastructure demand, not consumer—smartphone shipments down 14% 2026, but hyperscaler capex $700-900B guides insulate server DRAM/NAND.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-9,1-21">SK Hynix leads HBM market with 50-55% share, Samsung 35-40%, Micron 5-10%</cite>, though <cite index="5-2,5-10">SK Hynix holds ~62% per recent estimates</cite>. <cite index="3-8,3-17">HBM3E accounts for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments through 2026; HBM4 in meaningful volume only from Q3 2026 onward</cite>. <cite index="1-8">Stack pricing: HBM3 ~$200, HBM3E ~$300, HBM4 ~$500 (estimated)</cite>. <cite index="3-9,3-10,3-11">Samsung moved quickly to exploit SK Hynix's measured HBM4 approach, mass-producing HBM4 from February 12, 2026, with cumulative revenue exceeding $1.2 billion by end-June</cite>. <cite index="5-25,5-27">All three suppliers passed NVIDIA HBM4 certification for Vera Rubin accelerator on June 5, 2026, but SK Hynix remains primary supplier by wide margin</cite>. <cite index="8-11,8-14,8-16">Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron accelerating 16-Hi HBM4 development for NVIDIA Q4 2026 delivery</cite>, overcoming stacking and thermal challenges within 775μm JEDEC spec.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix stocks plunge 9-15% Thursday on Nasdaq tech selloff
news_pulse.implication: Broad risk-off in semis; both names erased billions in market cap. Tests conviction into Samsung earnings 7/8 and SK ADR debut 7/10.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix delays HBM3E-to-HBM4 conversion, retooling lines for DDR5 to capture 90% margins
news_pulse.implication: SK prioritizing near-term profitability over HBM4 capacity race. Extends HBM3E dominance but cedes HBM4 first-mover to Samsung. Bullish for DDR5 ASP persistence, neutral-to-negative for HBM4 supply elasticity.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung HBM4 cumulative revenue crosses $1B in 4 months, on track for $1.2B+ by end-June
news_pulse.implication: Monetization velocity confirms Samsung's HBM4 ramp is commercially live, not just qualification theater. Closes revenue gap with SK Hynix faster than consensus expected.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex guidance 2026: $700-900B aggregate, up 36% YoY; ~75% AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Demand backdrop intact. MSFT $120B+, AMZN $200B, META raised to $125-145B. Memory buyers locked in multi-quarter contracts; spot fatigue doesn't break contract cycle until 2027 fab capacity hits.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15%—decelerating but not reversing
news_pulse.implication: Parabolic phase maturing; buyers hitting affordability limits but AI server demand keeps floor under pricing. Consumer demand destruction (smartphones -14%, notebook downgrades) offset by enterprise SSD / RDIMM pull.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity 120-130K wpm by end-2026, 10x vs end-2023; NVIDIA reserves >60% through 2027
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains binding constraint on AI chip supply. CoWoS-L (LSI bridge) enabling NVIDIA B200/Rubin + AMD MI300X/MI400. Every HBM accelerator depends on this bottleneck—no relief until Arizona fabs online 2028+.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ADR listing July 10 on Nasdaq; underwriting fee ~0.5%, potential $29B offering
news_pulse.implication: Largest ADR offering ever if executed at scale. Unlocks U.S. institutional access, potential valuation re-rating vs. Samsung. HSBC raised PT to 4M won (+38%) on 20% premium for global investor access.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung + SK Hynix combined market cap exceeds South Korea's 2025 GDP (3.54 quadrillion won vs 2.68 quadrillion)
news_pulse.implication: Concentration risk flagged by domestic press. Retail owns only 13% of Samsung shares. Signals froth but also structural shift: memory transitioned from commodity to strategic asset with pricing power.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures vol elevated post-Thursday drawdown. Options flow likely skewed protective (puts) into Samsung earnings 7/8 and SK ADR 7/10. If Samsung prints ≥90T won and SK ADR draws strong U.S. demand, implied vol collapse benefits call sellers. Watch KOSPI sector rotation: if semis rally, financials/industrials likely lag. USD/KRW stability (currently ~1,530) critical—ADR pricing arbitrage sensitive to FX slippage.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung Q2 prelim earnings release Tuesday 7/8 pre-market KST—consensus 86T won op profit, upside case 90T+; any HBM4 revenue/allocation color
SK Hynix ADR debut volume/pricing 7/10 Nasdaq open—test of U.S. institutional appetite and valuation premium vs. KRX
Hyperscaler earnings commentary (MSFT, GOOGL, META) through July for capex reaffirmation or trim signals
July spot DRAM/NAND pricing from TrendForce/DRAMeXchange—confirm Q3 deceleration trajectory or surprise upside
TSMC Q2 earnings 7/18 for CoWoS capacity update and HBM customer allocation shifts
